newsitem.title: USA: Ill. tollway challengers to seek injunction.
newsitem.headline: Ill. tollway challengers to seek injunction.

text.p: Toll payers challenging the Illinois State Toll Highway Authority budget process will ask a state judge on Wednesday to enjoin it from most expenditures excluding debt service and road repairs, an attorney for the plaintiffs said.
Tollway funding challengers filed an injunction request about a year ago and reiterated their claims in an appearance Tuesday before Cook County Judge Stephen Schiller, attorney Lee Schwartz said.

Schiller scheduled an injunction hearing for Wednesday afternoon on the request to require the toll authority to hold the tolls it collects in escrow until a final decision is reached in the matter, Schwartz said.
The injunction would permit payments for continuing debt service, police services and road repairs, Schwartz said.
Schiller last week held that the toll authority's decades old practice of making continuing appropriations without oversight of the governor or General Assembly violated the Illinois Constitution.

State law permits the authority to make continuing appropriations for the repayment of a multiyear finite debt, but does not give "unfettered" power to spend tolls it collects in any manner it sees fit, Schiller found.
A spokesman for the authority has said it will appeal that ruling.
The Environmental Law & Policy Center supported failed legislation requiring oversight of the authority and was pleased with Schiller's ruling, spokesman Mike Truppa said.
Governmental or legislative oversight would not be drastic or onerous for the authority, Truppa said.
The center would prefer that a court order require the authority to stop collecting tolls and begin expending an estimated $400 million surplus, Truppa said.
